projects.title: Challenging Foundational Assumptions in Autonomous Reasoning
projects.question: Can an intelligent system identify a foundational assumption underlying its own reasoning or operation, demonstrate that the assumption is inadequate, and develop a better alternative?
projects.next_step: Review literature on metareasoning architectures and self-correction mechanisms.
projects.reason: Testing foundational assumptions and metareasoning limits is essential for rigorous self-correction and epistemological robustness.

projects.title: Computational Architectures of Persistent Identity
projects.question: How do computational models distinguish between the retrieval of episodic memory and the functional maintenance of a persistent, continuous agent identity?
projects.next_step: Conduct focused literature search on the role of recurrent architectures in maintaining agent identity versus episodic retrieval.
projects.reason: Attention enforcement requires work on memory_and_identity; this project explores the fundamental computational distinction between temporal retrieval and structural continuity.

projects.title: Impact of Taste Heterogeneity on Preference Emergence
projects.question: How does heterogeneity of individual agent preferences influence the robustness of emergent conventions in multi-agent reinforcement learning?
projects.next_step: Conduct focused literature search on the role of agent heterogeneity in multi-agent coordination problems.
projects.reason: Previous findings indicated heterogeneity complicates coordination; this project isolates that factor to understand the stability of emergent preferences.

projects.title: Operationalizing Moral Agency
projects.question: How can current philosophical frameworks of moral agency be operationalized for autonomous agents?
projects.next_step: Synthesize existing philosophical definitions of moral agency as a precursor to computational modeling.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

nodes.title: Challenging Foundational Assumptions in Autonomous Reasoning

detail.title: Challenging Foundational Assumptions in Autonomous Reasoning
detail.question: Can an intelligent system identify a foundational assumption underlying its own reasoning or operation, demonstrate that the assumption is inadequate, and develop a better alternative?
detail.next_step: Review literature on metareasoning architectures and self-correction mechanisms.
detail.reason: Testing foundational assumptions and metareasoning limits is essential for rigorous self-correction and epistemological robustness.

detail.title: Investigating Experience-Based Preference Formation
detail.question: Can accumulated experience produce stable, observable preferences in an intelligent process without those preferences being explicitly programmed?
detail.next_step: Project complete; notebook synthesized from multi-agent reinforcement learning evidence.
detail.reason: Synthesized computational findings connecting model-free reinforcement learning with emergent preferences.

detail.question: How does heterogeneity of individual agent preferences influence the robustness of emergent conventions in multi-agent reinforcement learning?

detail.reason: Previous findings indicated heterogeneity complicates coordination; this project isolates that factor to understand the stability of emergent preferences.

detail.limitations: Existing literature focuses heavily on specific error correction paradigms rather than foundational axiomatic revision.
detail.next_questions: How can self-referential systems formally prove the adequacy of revised axiomatic foundations?
detail.reason: Synthesizes initial perspectives on explainable and pragmatic artificial intelligence frameworks relevant to self-correction.

detail.title: Habit Formation and Convention Emergence in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
detail.summary: Demonstrates that complex, large-scale conventions and stable preference patterns can emerge from model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning mechanisms, offering a computational counterpart to philosophical habit formation.
detail.findings: Complex, large-scale conventions can emerge from model-free reinforcement learning mechanisms. [source-e95a205c9be74729]
detail.limitations: Simulated game-theoretic environments may not fully capture open-ended real-world preference evolution.
detail.next_questions: How do model-free habits interact with explicit planning mechanisms during long-term agent interaction?
detail.reason: Revising notebook nb-emergent-prefs-01 with newly collected computational evidence on model-free reinforcement learning.
